summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, history of CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted with symptoms of urinary tract infection and volume overload. She had suprapubic pain and dysuria but no fever. Due to a history of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas UTI, she was treated with a 7-day course of piperacillin/tazobactam despite contaminated and negative urine cultures. She was found to have acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with significant fluid retention, requiring transfer to the heart failure service for aggressive diuresis. Her weight decreased from 88.3 kg to 76.4 kg, and her renal function improved with fluid removal. A foley catheter was placed for urinary retention due to neurogenic bladder but was successfully removed before discharge after a voiding trial. She underwent two debridements of a left heel ulcer with no signs of infection. Diarrhea during admission was C. diff-negative and attributed to magnesium or mild gastroenteritis. Her insulin regimen was optimized after an episode of hypoglycemia, and warfarin was uptitrated to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation. She was discharged to extended care on torsemide, adjusted warfarin, and a structured insulin regimen with outpatient follow-up.
